title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: Recognition, Assessment and Shared-Care Follow-Up

evidenceAudit.scope: Children, young people and adults with possible attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in primary care, paediatrics and psychiatry: recognition, referral, who diagnoses, pre-medicine baseline, first-line medicines for Saudi Arabia, monitoring and shared care. Uses the Saudi ADHD Society clinical practice guideline (adapted from NICE NG87) and product information.
findings: Rebuilt from the thin 21 Oct 2026 version: presentation, cardiology referral triggers, monitoring intervals, six management steps and a Saudi source added.

Saudi correction: lisdexamfetamine was not SFDA-approved when the Saudi guideline was published, so methylphenidate is the preferred adult first-line medicine and lisdexamfetamine is an alternative; atomoxetine added as the non-stimulant option.
Doses trace to product information opened on 22 Oct 2026.
unverifiedSections: The Saudi guideline lists lisdexamfetamine or methylphenidate for adults without ranking; methylphenidate is marked preferred because of Saudi registration at publication. Current SFDA status not checked.
DSM-5 symptom counts and age-of-onset thresholds are not stated in the Saudi summary booklet and are not given here.
Paediatric atomoxetine and methylphenidate rows follow UK product information; the Saudi National Formulary governs local titration (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.27).
Normal values for rating scales are descriptive; scales are not diagnostic.
Distinguishing features for differentials are clinical descriptions not taken from an opened guideline section.

pathophysiology.summary: ADHD is a neurodevelopmental condition of inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity that causes impairment in two or more settings (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 3.3, p. 21). Diagnosis uses the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual, fifth edition (DSM-5) or International Classification of Diseases, eleventh revision (ICD-11) criteria and needs at least moderate impairment (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 3.3, p. 21). Stimulants raise heart rate and blood pressure and can slow growth, which drives the monitoring schedule (Concerta XL SmPC, Section 4.4).
keyMechanisms: Core features: inattention, hyperactivity, impulsivity (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 3.3, p. 21).
Impairment must be pervasive — two or more settings (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 3.3, p. 21).
Stimulants increase pulse and blood pressure (Concerta XL SmPC, Section 4.4).
Stimulants can reduce appetite and growth in children (Concerta XL SmPC, Section 4.4).

symptoms: Inattention: poor focus, disorganisation, forgetfulness (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 3.3, p. 21).
Hyperactivity: restlessness, excessive movement (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 3.3, p. 21).
Impulsivity: acting without thinking, interrupting (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 3.3, p. 21).
Functional impairment at home and at school or work (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 3.3, p. 21).
physicalSigns: Height and weight plotted on centile charts at baseline (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.3, p. 30).
Baseline pulse and blood pressure (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.3, p. 30).
Cardiac murmur or signs of heart failure — cardiology opinion before medicine (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.4, p. 31).
Blood pressure consistently above the 95th centile in a child — hypertension referral (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.5, p. 31).
redFlags: Exertional fainting or breathlessness, or sudden regular palpitations (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.4, p. 31).
Sudden cardiac death in a first-degree relative under 40 years (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.4, p. 31).
On treatment: resting pulse over 120/min, arrhythmia or systolic blood pressure above the 95th centile twice — reduce dose and refer (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 8.11, p. 36).
Suicidal thinking, psychosis or mania (Concerta XL SmPC, Section 4.3).
precipitants: Substance misuse risk to assess before treatment (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.3, p. 30).
Coexisting mental health, social or educational problems (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.3, p. 30).
Coexisting neurodevelopmental or physical conditions slow titration (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.28, p. 33).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Social-communication difference and restricted interests dominate; may coexist with ADHD.
Restlessness and poor focus track mood or worry episodes rather than starting in childhood.
Daytime inattention with poor or disrupted sleep.
Inattention limited to tasks beyond ability or hearing; improves when addressed.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Specialist psychiatrist, specialist paediatrician, trained family physician or other qualified professional (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 3.1, p. 21).
DSM-5 or ICD-11 criteria, at least moderate impairment, present in two or more settings (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 3.3, p. 21).
Support but do not replace diagnosis (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 3.2, p. 21).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: DSM-5 or ICD-11 criteria with moderate impairment in two or more settings

clinicalManagement.title: Recognise and support
actions: Record symptoms, settings, impairment, development, sleep, mental health and substance use.
Under 5 years: offer an ADHD-focused group parent-training programme first (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 5.7, p. 26).

clinicalManagement.title: Refer for diagnosis
actions: Refer to a qualified professional for diagnosis (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 3.1, p. 21).
Send home and school or work reports.

clinicalManagement.title: Baseline before medicine
actions: Height, weight, pulse, blood pressure and cardiovascular history (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.3, p. 30).
Cardiology opinion for any Recommendation 7.4 feature (see Red flags).

clinicalManagement.title: Start first-line treatment
actions: Children 5 years and over: parent support plus methylphenidate (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendations 5.10 and 7.6, pp. 26 and 31).
Adults: methylphenidate in Saudi Arabia; lisdexamfetamine only where registered (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, pp. 32 and 46).
Under 5 years: no medicine without a second specialist opinion, ideally tertiary (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 5.9, p. 26).

clinicalManagement.title: Monitor
actions: Pulse and blood pressure before and after each dose change and every 6 months (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 8.9, p. 36).
Height every 6 months; weight per Recommendation 8.5.
Pulse over 120/min, arrhythmia or systolic above the 95th centile twice: reduce dose and refer (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 8.11, p. 36).

clinicalManagement.title: Shared care and yearly review
actions: Shared care with primary care after titration (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.29, p. 34).
Trained clinician reviews medicine at least yearly (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 10.1, p. 39).

regimens.indication: ADHD, first-line medicine after specialist diagnosis
regimens.patientGroup: Child aged 6 years and over or young person with ADHD and persisting impairment
regimens.dose: Start 18 mg; increase in 18 mg steps about weekly
regimens.duration: Maximum 54 mg daily; titration typically 4–6 weeks (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, p. 47); review at least yearly
adjustments: Specialist starts and titrates; shared care with primary care only after stabilisation (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.29, p. 34).
Controlled drug: prescribe under Saudi MOH narcotic and psychotropic regulations (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 7.25, p. 34).

Authorised in Saudi Arabia at guideline publication (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, p. 46); SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so Saudi registration was not verified; check the register and the hospital formulary before prescribing.
Paediatric: This row gives the paediatric dose (children 6 years and over; the Saudi guideline notes off-label use at 5–6 years).
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic — penicillin allergy does not affect this medicine.
CKD: Not studied in renal impairment; no dose guidance (Concerta XL SmPC, Section 4.2).
CLD: Not studied in hepatic impairment; no dose guidance (Concerta XL SmPC, Section 4.2).
monitoring: Pulse and blood pressure on a centile chart at each dose change and at least every 6 months (Concerta XL SmPC, Section 4.4).
Height every 6 months; weight every 3 months at age 10 and under (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 8.5, p. 35).
Psychiatric symptoms at each dose change and at least every 6 months (Concerta XL SmPC, Section 4.4).
contraindications: Glaucoma; phaeochromocytoma; hyperthyroidism; monoamine oxidase inhibitor within 14 days (Concerta XL SmPC, Section 4.3).
Severe depression, anorexia nervosa, suicidal tendency, psychosis, mania or poorly controlled bipolar I disorder (Concerta XL SmPC, Section 4.3).
Pre-existing cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disorders (Concerta XL SmPC, Section 4.3).

regimens.dose: Up to 70 kg: start about 0.5 mg/kg/day for at least 7 days, maintenance about 1.2 mg/kg/day; over 70 kg: start 40 mg/day, maintenance 80 mg/day
regimens.duration: Maximum 100 mg/day over 70 kg; review at least yearly
adjustments: Later-line option in the Saudi guideline (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendations 7.7–7.9, pp. 31–32); authorised in Saudi Arabia at publication (p. 46).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so Saudi registration was not verified; check the register and the hospital formulary before prescribing.
Paediatric: This row gives the paediatric dose (children 6 years and over; the Saudi guideline notes off-label use at 5–6 years).
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic — penicillin allergy does not affect this medicine.
CKD: No dose change, including end-stage renal disease (Strattera SmPC, Section 4.2).
CLD: Child-Pugh B: halve the starting and target dose; Child-Pugh C: 25% of the usual dose (Strattera SmPC, Section 4.2).
monitoring: Suicidal thinking, especially in children and adolescents (Strattera SmPC, Section 4.4).
Stop for jaundice or laboratory evidence of liver injury; do not restart (Strattera SmPC, Section 4.4).
Pulse, blood pressure and growth as for methylphenidate (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 8.5, p. 35).
contraindications: Monoamine oxidase inhibitor within 2 weeks; narrow-angle glaucoma; severe cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disorder; phaeochromocytoma (Strattera SmPC, Section 4.3).

regimens.dose: Start 30 mg (20 mg if a lower start is appropriate); increase by 10–20 mg about weekly
regimens.duration: Maximum 70 mg/day; stop if no improvement after dose adjustment over 1 month (Elvanse SmPC, Section 4.2)
adjustments: Not SFDA-approved when the Saudi guideline was published (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, pp. 46 and 51); check current registration before use.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so Saudi registration was not verified; check the register and the hospital formulary before prescribing.
Paediatric: Adult row; not recommended under 6 years (Elvanse SmPC, Section 4.2).
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic — penicillin allergy does not affect this medicine.
CKD: Severe impairment (glomerular filtration rate 15 to under 30 mL/min/1.73 m²): maximum 50 mg/day; consider further reduction on dialysis (Elvanse SmPC, Section 4.2).
CLD: No studies; no dose recommendation (Elvanse SmPC, Section 4.2).
monitoring: Pulse and blood pressure before and after each dose change and every 6 months (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 8.9, p. 36).
Weight every 6 months in adults (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendation 8.5, p. 35).
contraindications: Monoamine oxidase inhibitor within 14 days; hyperthyroidism; agitated states; symptomatic cardiovascular disease; advanced arteriosclerosis; moderate to severe hypertension; glaucoma (Elvanse SmPC, Section 4.3).

medicationPlan.note: Choose one medicine per patient. Specialist starts and titrates; primary care continues only under shared care. Stimulants are controlled drugs under Saudi MOH regulations. Paediatric, penicillin-allergy (not applicable), chronic kidney disease (CKD) and chronic liver disease (CLD) lines are on every row. SFDA registration not verified in this task.

values: First-line option for adults and children 5+

learningObjectives: Know who may diagnose ADHD in Saudi Arabia.
Complete the pre-medicine baseline and cardiology screen.
Run the monitoring schedule in shared care.
keyPoints: Rating scales support but never make the diagnosis.
Methylphenidate is the Saudi first-line medicine at all ages from 5.
pitfalls: Starting a stimulant without growth and blood pressure baseline.
Prescribing lisdexamfetamine without checking Saudi registration.

patientEducation: Explain ADHD, treatment options and that medicine is one part of care.
Explain side effects to report: palpitations, fainting, mood change, poor appetite.
lifestyleAndDiet: Record appetite and weight at every review; stimulants can reduce appetite and growth (Concerta XL SmPC, Section 4.4).
mdtReferrals: Child and adolescent psychiatry or paediatrics
Cardiology when Recommendation 7.4 features are present
dischargeCriteria: Not an acute condition; shared-care responsibilities documented and a named contact given.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Pulse and blood pressure every 6 months; height every 6 months in children; weight per age band; medicine review at least yearly (Saudi ADHD CPG 2020, Recommendations 8.5, 8.9 and 10.1).
